newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Rato sees 240,000 new jobs created in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Rato sees 240,000 new jobs created in 1997.

text.p: Spain's Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Wednesday he expected some 240,000 jobs to be created in 1997, but reforms were vital to secure job creation in the longer-term.
"Unemployment is clearly a very serious problem in Spain...but we are creating jobs at a much greater rate than before and a greater rate than other European countries," Rato told state television.

"I expect that if things continue as they are, we shall see the creation of 240,000 jobs in 1997 and we will continue in 1998 and we will continue to strive to fix our worst problem, which is unemployment," he added.

"It is important that we make reforms...and our unions and employers have shown that they are capable of understanding each other and reaching an agreement...which in other European countries has proved impossible," he said.

Spain's unions and employers finished drafting an agreement on labour reforms earlier in April and expect to sign the deal next Monday. The government will then study ways of converting the proposals into legislation.
